topics.title: Barry’s Drug Investigation & Airport Pee
topics.summary: Following an investigation involving cocaine found in Barry’s room and subsequent questioning, he claims to be fighting for a drug-free society. Simultaneously, the show discusses Jack Spector's abrupt departure from NBC after urinating on an airline galley, with no further details provided.

topics.title: Jack Spector’s Phone Call Mishap
topics.summary: During a radio segment, Jack Spector fields bizarre phone calls from listeners. He engages in bets with Gary regarding his airtime duration, recounts attempts to leverage him for sports knowledge or personal favors, and reflects on the fleeting nature of fame after transitioning off NBC.”} 39 words”} 102 words

topics.title: Stern’s Repeated Calls to Spector
topics.summary: Howard recounts his persistent attempts to contact Jack Spector on his show, detailing how he repeatedly called despite being rejected and hung up upon. He describes pretending to be a caller himself, driving Spector crazy with inquiries before securing an agent position after an audition.

topics.title: Radio Host Discussions and Confusion
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts discuss Meg Capon’s recent relationship with Steve Capen, including her apparent attraction and awkward interactions. They share anecdotes about previous relationships and offer advice on navigating romantic connections while discussing potential suitors for Meg.

topics.title: Radio Host Ramblings
topics.summary: A long-form monologue features a radio host recounting bizarre personal experiences including professional failures, strange encounters with strangers, and increasingly outlandish fantasies about his neighbor Meg. The conversation shifts rapidly between anecdotes and absurd speculation without clear narrative structure.

topics.title: Stern’s Accusations and Telethon Interference
topics.summary: Howard Stern discusses a fabricated story in "Gentlemen's Quarterly Magazine" accusing him of inappropriate behavior during his husband’s mourning period, offering a $5,000 reward for the author’s identity. He then recounts an incident involving Gary interfering with a Ramones telethon and Janet Culver drinking her own urine.”} 39 words”**
